# grimoire-amix

> Developer- and LLM-oriented documentation for **Amiga Unix (Amix)** — Commodore's port of AT&T
> System V Release 4 (SVR4) to 68030 Amigas (A3000UX / A2500UX), extended by a community 68040/68060
> port; the amigaux 1.0 release ships it for 68060 Amigas with a Z3660 and as a classic 68030 kit.
> It explains how Amix works, how to develop software and device drivers for it, and how to build
> custom boot/install disks with extra hardware drivers. Independent of, and cross-linked to,
> amigaunix.com; we go deeper on development.

The single source of truth (facts + citations + ✅/🟡/🔴 confidence tags) is
[research-brief.md](sources/research-brief.md). Contributor rules are in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
For the full corpus in one file, see [llms-full.txt](llms-full.txt).

## How Amix works
- [What Amix Is](docs/how-it-works/overview.md): SVR4/3B2 lineage, what it is and isn't, version timeline.
- [Supported Hardware & Requirements](docs/how-it-works/hardware.md): machines, MMU/FPU, the Fast RAM envelope (4 MB minimum; a 16 MB A3000 motherboard bank for the stock kernel; 128 MB on the 040/060 kernels), SCSI ID rules, Zorro II only.
- [The Amix RAM Ceiling](docs/how-it-works/ram-ceiling.md): the separate total-describable-RAM limit (≈64 MB on a stock 030 kernel with 2 KiB pages, set by a fixed 4 MiB kernel arena; ≈128 MB on the 4 KiB-page 040/060 kernels — the same for a 68040 and a 68060, measured on the 060) — an unchecked rmalloc in page_init wild-writes from address 0, silently; detection fingerprint and RAM guidance for emulators and real hardware.
- [Amix on 68040 and 68060 — Current Status](docs/how-it-works/68040-68060-status.md): why stock Amix is 030-only, the public 68040/68060 port (asokero/amix-040-060-port, since 2026-09-19) and what it reports, the FPU-less 68LC060 lane, and what not to claim.
- [How Amix Boots](docs/how-it-works/boot-process.md): Superkickstart → bootblock → compressed kernel; RDB layout; what the Kickstart strap checks in a bootblock (`DOS` + checksum only; `UNI\0` = no bootblock), the AN_BootError reset loop, loader-writer notes (trackdisk cache, chip-RAM speed, AGA state), and CD boot through an A4091/A4092 ROM (ISO9660 node, AmigaDOS startup-sequence).
- [Kernel Architecture](docs/how-it-works/kernel-architecture.md): monolithic SVR4, /usr/sys, switch tables, MMU, STREAMS.
- [Filesystems & Disk Layout](docs/how-it-works/filesystems-and-disks.md): RDB partitions, UFS vs s5, /dev disk naming.
- [Networking](docs/how-it-works/networking.md): STREAMS TCP/IP, A2065, DNS-off default, gethostbyname without dotted quads, NFS, SLIP, and the stock 4 KB TCP lower-read queue that silently drops inbound bursts.
- [X11 & the Desktop](docs/how-it-works/x11-and-desktop.md): X11R4/R5, OpenLook, A2410 color, RTG (X11R5 + X11R6.3 generations, Mesa 3.1).
- [Package Management](docs/how-it-works/package-management.md): the stock SVR4 pkg system — /var/sadm contents(4) DB, media formats, pkgadd mechanics, and a space-in-pathname defect that breaks pkgrm/pkginfo on the shipped image.
- [The Amix Package Repository Format](docs/how-it-works/package-repository.md): the canonical public host pkg.amigaux.org (plain HTTP for apkg), the static repo tree, the pipe-delimited catalog v1 grammar and names.conf, md5+size integrity, the apkg client's three sources (HTTP / mounted medium / raw slice), the two publish gates (owner-run publish, fail-closed licence gates) and the catalog-regenerate trap.
- [Quirks & Gotchas](docs/how-it-works/quirks.md): the Amiga-port surprises — 90 numbered items, from hard-coded SCSI IDs to the stock TCP 4 KB queue, the ftruncate shrink panic, syslogd's m4 dependency, the 2.1 sh read buffer, 4 KiB pages vs small-block filesystems, and the CIA-A timer Kickstart leaves running.
- [Emulation Fidelity](docs/how-it-works/emulation-fidelity.md): what a 68030/MMU/interrupt emulator must implement — format-$B bus-error frames, SCSI INT2 latency — or Amix's demand-paging boot fails, sometimes silently.
- [Z3660 board timings](docs/how-it-works/z3660-timings.md): CPLD clock rows are per-unit and per-clock — the laws, the 25.000 MHz edge, a two-card row-by-row campaign from the stock table (no shared usable rows; reset after every failing step; the 360° trap), and the config-vs-failing-card diagnostic.
- [Z3660 ethernet](docs/how-it-works/z3660-ethernet.md): the card's receive path (GEM descriptors, firmware backlog, the ~1 ms interrupt nag), the MAC-write ring-offset trap, the five z3660cfg.txt ethernet keys, reading the GEM counters, and measured Amix vs AmigaOS (AmiTCP_NG, PrismNet) throughput.
- [Load averages](docs/how-it-works/load-averages.md): why uptime and w print garbage (two independent stock defects) and how to read the real value.
- [Performance benchmarks](docs/how-it-works/performance-benchmarks.md): measured Dhrystone, sequential disk-I/O and CPU-temperature figures for Amix on real and emulated 68k, with the method behind each set of numbers.
- [Glossary](docs/how-it-works/glossary.md): terms used across the docs.

## Getting started (emulation-first)
- [Running Amix in WinUAE](docs/getting-started/emulation-winuae.md): the exact config (MMU on, JIT off, SCSI 6/4).
- [Running Amix in FS-UAE](docs/getting-started/emulation-fs-uae.md): the verified FS-UAE config.
- [Amix on Amiberry](docs/getting-started/emulation-amiberry.md): Amiberry (8.3.0 or newer) fully runs AND installs Amix — its A3000 on-board SCSI emulates the disk (ID 6) and tape (ID 4); plus real A2065 networking.
- [Putting Amix on your real LAN (Amiberry)](docs/getting-started/networking-on-the-lan.md): verified recipe — A2065 on a routed TAP + proxy-ARP; static IP, gateway, DNS, internet, reachable inbound, persistent at boot.
- [Installing Amix (Walkthrough)](docs/getting-started/install-walkthrough.md): boot+root+tape → partition → kernel → patch.
- [Running Amix on Real Hardware](docs/getting-started/real-hardware.md): A3000UX/A2500UX, modern SCSI.
- [First Login & a Quick Tour](docs/getting-started/first-login-and-tour.md): login, consoles, shells, X.

## Driver & software development
- [The Amix Device-Driver Model](docs/drivers/driver-model.md): major/minor, cdevsw/bdevsw switch tables.
- [Building & Installing a Kernel](docs/drivers/kernel-build.md): /usr/sys, kernel.c, make, make bootpart.
- [Composing Multi-Driver Kernels](docs/drivers/kernel-composition.md): why one kernel per root-storage family beats a universal all-drivers image — SDCARDS=2, the card-0 address sort vs the compiled-in rootdev, probe safety, the driver admission checklist, and the whole-kernel-package delivery path.
- [Loadable Kernel Modules (amigaux 1.1, in development)](docs/drivers/loadable-modules.md): the module system being built for 1.1 in amigaux/amix (own boot loader, MIT DLM core, kbootset generations, the ABI kit and kabi rule, root/boot/demand classes, the static floor, safe mode), the kernel facts every driver author needs (no spl masks level 6, STREAMS opens at level 4, the kmem budget per line, board windows, DMA calls), and what is proven where as of 2026-10-29.
- [Reverse-engineering the prebuilt kernel](docs/drivers/kernel-reverse-engineering.md): disassembling the source-free /usr/sys/*/exp objects + reading globals from a savestate; worked on the mount(2)/vfssw fstype path (an errno-22 from `mount -F <fs>` = fstype not live in the booted kernel).
- [Writing a Character Driver](docs/drivers/writing-a-char-driver.md): the Ditto par.c walkthrough.
- [Writing a STREAMS/DLPI Driver](docs/drivers/writing-a-streams-driver.md): network drivers via hydra.
- [Zorro II AUTOCONFIG for Drivers](docs/drivers/zorro-autoconfig.md): autocon(), board IDs, /dev/mem scanning.
- [X11 RTG Graphics Drivers](docs/drivers/x11-rtg-drivers.md): an X server over a kernel framebuffer driver — two generations: Xrtg/VA2000 (X11R5) and Xzz9000/ZZ9000 (X11R6.3).
- [Toolchain & Packaging](docs/drivers/toolchain.md): native cc/gcc; gcc-cross-amix (GCC 2.7.2.3, m68k-cbm-sysv4) for kernel space and gcc14-cross-amix (GCC 14.2, m68k-elf) for userland — AMIX's return convention (pointers in %a0 and %d0, structs in memory) and -malign-int (sizeof(FILE) 16) as ABI, the specs, the 68060 check, known libc/X11 defects; the sysroot's patch level (patch 2a changes three headers and make); libc porting gaps (vfork, sigaltstack, snprintf, ftruncate); the stock libm.a (software math, fmovecr/fintrz traps on 040/060, SVID errors); elf2brel, pkgadd.
- [Case Study: va2000-amix](docs/drivers/case-studies/va2000.md): char framebuffer driver (MNT VA2000).
- [Case Study: xrtg-amix](docs/drivers/case-studies/xrtg.md): X11R5 server for the VA2000.
- [Case Study: lszorro-amix](docs/drivers/case-studies/lszorro.md): userspace Zorro II scanner.
- [Case Study: hydra-amix](docs/drivers/case-studies/hydra.md): STREAMS/DLPI Ethernet driver.
- [Case Study: zz9000-amix](docs/drivers/case-studies/zz9000.md): kernel framebuffer driver for the MNT ZZ9000 (Zorro II product 3; /dev/zz9000 char major 49) — mode setting, mmap, ioctl API, late-activated ANSI framebuffer console; the foundation of the X11R6.3 RTG stack.
- [Case Study: x11r6.3-amix (Xzz9000)](docs/drivers/case-studies/x11r63-zz9000.md): an X11R6.3 port whose Xzz9000 server drives /dev/zz9000 through a card-generic RTG DDX layer; documents the native Amix shared-library ABI (ld -G -h runtime images + .sa stub archives, strict link order).
- [Case Study: mesa-amix (Mesa 3.1)](docs/drivers/case-studies/mesa31.md): OpenGL on Amix — Mesa 3.1 software rendering via the Xlib driver against Xzz9000; static libGL/GLU/glut bootstrap, no server-side GLX.
- [Case Study: A4091 / 53C710 SCSI driver](docs/drivers/a4091-53c710-driver.md): booting Amix from a Zorro III A4091 — the 68030 TT-gap obstacle, sptalloc, the 53C710 SCRIPTS driver, and chipset-gated auto-detection (emulation-proven); Zorro III DMA into Z3660 RAM on real hardware, the A4092 CPLD 1.4.21 CTEST8.SM bus-grant gate and other 53C710 behaviours, the A4000T onboard 53C710 (fixed $DD0000, readable only after the ROM's NCR driver), and why a Z3660 in 68030 mode cannot do bus-master DMA.
- [Case Study: Z3660 ethernet driver (zen0)](docs/drivers/z3660-ethernet-driver.md): native SVR4 STREAMS/DLPI driver for the Z3660 accelerator's onboard Zynq ethernet — the firmware frame-mailbox protocol, polled RX (no int2_tbl), the INT6 interrupt-storm fix; full bidirectional TCP/IP on real hardware (A4000 + Z3660, 2026-06).
- [Case Study: Z3660 piscsi SCSI driver (z3660.c)](docs/drivers/z3660-scsi-driver.md): the Z3660's onboard "SCSI" is not a SCSI chip but the PiStorm piscsi register mailbox ported to its Zynq ARM — a ~5-poke synchronous block driver, the multi-method detect that cleared a silent hang, and the firmware-emulator bug that masqueraded as a driver hang; booted Amix multiuser with root on real hardware (A4000 + Z3660, 2026-06), first try; the FPGA address-capture race (back-to-back accesses landing at previous AND current address) and the arm-every-write rule; the 68060 cache arm.

## Custom boot & install disks
- [Anatomy of the Boot Floppy](docs/boot-disks/anatomy-boot-adf.md): bootblock + compressed kernel.
- [Anatomy of the Root (miniroot) Floppy](docs/boot-disks/anatomy-root-adf.md): the s5 miniroot — installer binaries + scripts (the UFS label is a string-heuristic artefact).
- [Anatomy of the Patch Floppy](docs/boot-disks/anatomy-patch-adf.md): self-extracting sh + cpio.
- [Reverse-Engineering the Boot Floppy](docs/boot-disks/reverse-engineering-boot-adf.md): the kernel is Unix compress/LZW → m68k ELF; the checksum is non-fatal; how to extract and rebuild.
- [Adding Drivers to a Custom Boot Disk](docs/boot-disks/adding-drivers-to-boot-disk.md): three delivery surfaces (boot partition, bootable floppy, add-on disk).
- [The Boot-Disk Tooling Pipeline](docs/boot-disks/build-pipeline.md): inspect / extract-kernel / build-bootfloppy / unpack / build scripts.

## Reference
- [Version Matrix](docs/reference/versions.md): Commodore versions 1.1 to 2.1c, the stock kernels by sha256, and why amigaux release numbers (1.0, 1.1) are not Commodore's.
- [Device & Card Reference](docs/reference/device-list.md)
- [Major-Number Registry](docs/reference/major-number-registry.md): every known cdevsw/bdevsw/vfssw/AutoConfig claim across the community trees — the two live collisions, the free ranges (55–67, 69; 52–54 went to the 1.1 module line), and the conventions for adding a driver.
- [Command Cheat Sheet](docs/reference/commands-cheatsheet.md)
- [Bibliography & Sources](docs/reference/bibliography.md)

## Optional
- [amigaunix.com](https://www.amigaunix.com/doku.php/home): the established community wiki (end-user/install/history).
- [amigaux/amix](https://github.com/amigaux/amix): the amigaux project's monorepo (work in progress) — kernel/dlm (loadable modules: loader, core, kbootset, ABI kit, spec) and kernel/modules today; toolchain pins; the system-file manifest. [amigaux/amix-040-060-port](https://github.com/amigaux/amix-040-060-port): the organisation's fork of the 68040/68060 port. [asokero/gcc14-cross-amix](https://github.com/asokero/gcc14-cross-amix): the GCC 14 userland cross compiler. [jusii/gcc-cross-amix](https://github.com/jusii/gcc-cross-amix): the gcc-cross-amix fork the project pins.
- [va2000-amix](https://github.com/asokero/va2000-amix), [xrtg-amix](https://github.com/asokero/xrtg-amix), [lszorro-amix](https://github.com/asokero/lszorro-amix), [hydra-amix](https://github.com/isoriano1968/hydra-amix), [zz9000-amix](https://github.com/isoriano1968/zz9000-amix), [x11r6.3-amix](https://github.com/isoriano1968/x11r6.3-amix), [mesa-amix](https://github.com/isoriano1968/mesa-amix), [gcc-cross-amix](https://github.com/isoriano1968/gcc-cross-amix) (Linux cross-toolchain): the modern Amix driver, graphics-stack, and toolchain repos this project documents.
